title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Vigyan TECH 2026 initiative
body_text:
‘विज्ञान Tech’, a first of its kind national initiative was organized by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), on National Technology Day, 11 May 2026 at BRIC-National Institute of Immunology (BRIC-NII), N. Delhi. The purpose was to promote a whole-of- Government approach for science, technology and innovation.
The exhibition brought together the technological strengths of 14 Ministries and Departments of the Government of India with strong R&D linkages through their autonomous institutes and laboratories and more than 100 in-house developed technologies were showcased. Based on a “Whole-of-Government” approach, technologies were showcased across key sectors such as Space and Geospatial Technologies; Climate and Agri-Food Technologies; Biopharma and Health Technologies; Bioindustrial and Green Chemicals; Deep-tech Materials and Advanced Engineering Technologies; Electronics, Semiconductors and Energy; and Deep-Sea and Atmospheric Technologies. The event also saw the release of ‘TECH-संग्रह’, a compendium featuring nearly 300 technologies developed by the participating institutions. Many of these technologies have already been commercialized or licensed, while others are progressing toward deployment to support national development goals.
The event witnessed several technology transfers/licensing of technologies to industry. The details are as follows:
DBT- Biotechnology Research & Innovation Council ( DBT-BRIC )
Accelerated Crop Innovation Technology platform Active dried yeast technology Enzyme for optimised lignocellulosic degradation technology CleverCUP NCE for Inflammatory Bowel Diseases
Indian Council For Medical Research (ICMR)
Factor VIII Inhibitor Test for Haemophilia A Disorder PSP94 ELISA Multiplex Real-Time RT-PCR for Detection of Dengue Chikungunya and Zika Viruses
Council for Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR)
CSIR PRIMA ET-11, 100% electric compact tractor
Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)
Extruded Products technology Hybrid Green House Solar dryer Protein & Fiber rich Granola Bar
The following were also launched during the event:
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Indigenous Glacier Lake Bathymetry Survey Solution developed by C-DAC, Thiruvananthapuram
Council for Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR)
CSIR@100, a booklet outlining CSIR’s roadmap towards 2042 with a strong focus on deep-tech innovation, translational research, and technologies aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
The initiative served as a common strategic platform for knowledge exchange, technology showcasing and exploring opportunities to bridge the gap between laboratory research and industrial application. By bringing together various Ministries, policymakers, scientists, young researchers, industry leaders, and startup founders, the initiative strengthened connections across the innovation ecosystem and provided valuable insights into new opportunities for collaboration and innovation. This is a significant step towards breaking institutional silos as we embark on our journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047.
This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) for the Ministry of Science and Technology & Ministry of Earth Sciences Dr. Jitendra Singh in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.

NKR/AK/MJ/NM

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply, the Minister of State for Science & Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, informed Parliament about 'Vigyan Tech', a first-of-its-kind national initiative held on National Technology Day (11 May 2026) at BRIC-NII, New Delhi. Organized by the Department of Biotechnology, it showcased over 100 in-house technologies from 14 Ministries/Departments under a 'Whole-of-Government' approach, released a compendium ('TECH-संग्रह') of nearly 300 technologies, and saw multiple technology transfers/licensing deals and new product launches from institutions like DBT-BRIC, ICMR, CSIR, and MoFPI.
enrichment.context:
The event reflects the government's push to break institutional silos in India's science and technology ecosystem and accelerate translation of publicly-funded research into commercial and industrial applications, a persistent challenge in Indian R&D. It aligns with the broader Viksit Bharat 2047 vision and initiatives like Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) and the National Deep Tech Startup Policy, which aim to strengthen lab-to-market pathways and foster public-private collaboration in strategic sectors such as space, health biotech, green chemicals, semiconductors, and deep-sea technologies.

The Department of Biotechnology (DBT) and its umbrella body BRIC (Biotechnology Research & Innovation Council) have been central to India's biotech innovation push, including COVID-era vaccine development. This event's emphasis on technology transfer to industry (e.g., CSIR's electric tractor PRIMA ET-11, ICMR's diagnostic kits) illustrates the government's focus on converting research output into deployable products, a theme recurrent in India's S&T policy discourse, including the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy (STIP) framework and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' in critical technologies.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Vigyan Tech' initiative, discussed recently, was organized on National Technology Day by which Department?
options: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR)
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
prelims_questions.explanation: The release explicitly states that 'Vigyan Tech' was organized by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT) at BRIC-National Institute of Immunology, New Delhi.

prelims_questions.question: National Technology Day, on which the 'Vigyan Tech' event was held, is observed on which date each year?
prelims_questions.explanation: National Technology Day is observed on 11 May, commemorating the 1998 Pokhran-II nuclear tests; the release confirms the event was held on this date in 2026.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of a 'Whole-of-Government' approach in fostering science, technology and innovation in India, citing recent government initiatives.

India continues to face challenges in translating laboratory research into commercially viable technologies. Examine the institutional and policy measures needed to bridge this gap, with reference to recent government efforts.
